transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-10 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood CSM), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Marcus Holt (Redwood Impl Eng), Aisha Kaur (Starlake Head of AI), Ben Torres (Starlake Platform Eng), Lina Gomez (Starlake PM), Evan Park (Starlake Security)

Auto-generated summary (brief, may be imperfect):
Jordan opened with onboarding objectives and ran through high level timeline. Customer has strict data residency and KMS preference; will evaluate dedicated vs hosted. Technical team wants staging endpoint and a latency & cost baseline. Next steps include runbook, security questionnaire, and scheduling an architecture deep-dive.

Topics:
- Kickoff goals and success criteria
- Network connectivity and auth (SSO / SAML, KMS)
- Environment plan (staging, canary, prod)
- Minimal viable rollout and pilot scope (first 2 weeks)
- Observability & runbooks
- Security questionnaire and compliance needs

Action items (recap in call): Jordan to send runbook; Marcus to provision staging; customer to send prompts and security answers.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Okay great, thanks everyone for joining, um this is Jordan with Redwood, I'm the CSM working with Starlake on this onboarding. quick round table, who we got from the Starlake side?
[00:12] Aisha: Hi all, Aisha Kaur here, head of the AI org at Starlake. We'll be the primary stakeholders for model output quality and acceptance.
[00:18] Ben: Ben Torres, platform engineering. I'll handle network and infra.
[00:22] Lina: Lina Gomez, product, I'll own rollout schedule and metrics.
[00:26] Evan: Evan Park, security. I'll lead the compliance questionnaire and KMS decisions.
[00:30] Jordan: Awesome, and on our side Priya is here to do the technical deep dives and Marcus is doing implementation work.
[00:36] Priya: Hey everyone, thanks. uh quick note: we usually propose a 4 week ramp but we can compress the pilot. want to understand constraints first.
[00:46] Marcus: Hi all. I will be provisioning staging and running initial smoke tests.

[01:00] Jordan: So objective for today's call is three fold — align on success criteria, confirm connectivity and security gating items, and agree next week's plan. I'll also run through a lightweight onboarding playbook. Sound good?
[01:12] Aisha: Yes that works. Our top success criteria are: acceptable latency under 350ms 95th on short prompts, data never leaves our region for PII prompts, and ability to roll back to deterministic baseline.
[01:26] Jordan: Noted, 350ms 95 pctl, regional data residency and deterministic fallback. We'll capture that.

[01:40] Ben: On the network side — we need VPC peering or private link. Also firewall egress rules. What's your recommended approach?
[01:48] Priya: For Starlake use case we recommend Private Link or VPC peering depending on cloud provider. the private plane in Redwood Private will give you the most control; hosted with VPC egress is possible but it's more of a hybrid. small tradeoff: dedicated capacity gives lower tail latency and predictable throughput.
[02:12] Ben: How big is the difference in tail latency generally? ballpark is fine.
[02:18] Priya: Ballpark: dedicated can shave 50-150ms depending on batch behavior. If you have tight SLAs and steady traffic, dedicated is worth the commit. If bursty and cost-sensitive, hosted with fallback is fine.
[02:36] Evan: Do you have SOC2 reports and a standard security questionnaire? we'll want to see encryption at rest and KMS integration.
[02:44] Jordan: Yes we have SOC2 Type II and the security pack; I'll share the doc after the call. For KMS we support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) across our Private offering and in some dedicated configurations.
[02:58] Evan: Ok, preferred KMS is Thales but we'll list options.

[03:12] Lina: For rollout, we want a small pilot with 10k tokens/day and 3 named product use-cases first. How do you suggest we measure quality regressions?
[03:22] Priya: Good question. We recommend a small eval harness — we can take your top 50 prompts and establish pass/fail thresholds (precision, hallucination rate). Redwood Optimize can run regression alerts tied to those prompts.
[03:34] Aisha: We'll need to scrub prompts for PII before sharing. that's on us.

[03:50] Jordan: I'll include a template for the prompt set and a quick how-to for redactions in the runbook.

[04:05] Ben: about traffic routing and fallback — you mentioned model variants. we want automatic fallback but with observability. how are rollouts handled?
[04:14] Priya: Rollouts are done per route and you can do canary percentages, A/B tests, and automatic fallback to a smaller model or older version on elevated error rates. traces and token-level cost are visible in Console. there's a bit of hand off with telemetry setup but we can ship a basic dashboard quickly.

[04:40] Marcus: I'll stand up a staging endpoint in the same region and route test traffic. what's the auth method? API keys by default or SSO?
[04:50] Jordan: For staging we typically start with API keys scoped to an environment, then move to SSO/SAML + RBAC for prod. Evan, from security perspective is token-based first acceptable?
[05:02] Evan: Yes for staging. For prod we need SSO with SAML and fine-grained RBAC, audit logs retained for 1 year. Can you support that?
[05:12] Jordan: Yes, audit logs are available and retention can be discussed. We'll note 1 year as a requirement.

[05:24] [snip] (mid-call technical discussion, rough verbatim follows)
[05:30] Priya: Quick note on KV cache — sorry K V, sometimes transcript says K V — the runtime handles KV caching for persistent conversational sessions. For your product, we can enable prefix caching to reduce token cost on repeat queries. Need to confirm privacy rules for cached content.
[05:52] Ben: If we cache, we need TTL and ability to evict keys. is that configurable?
[05:58] Priya: Yes TTLs per route and manual eviction APIs are available. We'll include the API doc link in the runbook.

[06:12] Aisha: Another constraint — some of our prompts reference licensed internal data, we need to ensure no training on customer data and strong contractual clauses.
[06:20] Jordan: Redwood's platform explicitly provides data isolation and options to opt out of training on customer inputs for Private/Dedicated; I'll flag that in the legal / SLA doc we share.

[06:34] Lina: How about cost visibility? we need per-route and per-team cost breakdowns so product can be charged back.
[06:42] Jordan: Console will show token-level cost by route and you can tag requests. We'll provide sample tagging strategy in the runbook.

[07:00] Evan: Auditing — what IDS / network monitoring hooks do you expose? we want to integrate into our SIEM.
[07:08] Priya: We have webhook-based logs and can stream audit logs to your S3 or to PagerDuty. For SIEM you'll want the JSON event stream; we can provide schema.

[07:28] Marcus: For the staging handoff I'll need an IP range and the peering details; Ben can share the firewall rules. I'll post the staging credentials as a secure note.
[07:38] Ben: I'll prepare a firewall egress rule list and send to Marcus.

[07:46] Jordan: Timeline proposal: this week we do runbook + security questionnaire, Marcus provisions staging next week and we do an architecture deep-dive mid next week, then pilot starts week after with monitoring and a short eval. Does that align?
[07:58] Aisha: Sounds reasonable. I want the pilot to be no more than 2 weeks and then decision point.
[08:06] Jordan: we'll set the decision point and success metrics in the runbook (latency, quality, cost).

[08:20] (discussion about POC metrics and measurement)

[08:34] Priya: On the topic of benchmarks, we can supply a small benchmark harness to validate tail latency and token cost. note that on large context windows cost will increase, we'll provide quantization suggestions.
[08:50] Aisha: We may need quantized models for cost reasons; do you recommend a path?
[08:56] Priya: Yes, Redwood Optimize can propose quantization profiles per workload, and we can test on staging. typical path is start with FP16 hosted then evaluate 4-bit quantized model in dedicated or private for cost savings.

[09:12] Jordan: Any other items from the team?
[09:18] Lina: I'd like a one-page launch checklist for product managers.
[09:22] Jordan: We'll include that.
[09:24] Evan: I'll follow up with the security questionnaire; would prefer to use your standard template.
[09:28] Jordan: Great. I'll email the pack and runbook after this call.

[09:36] (wrap up)
[09:38] Jordan: Okay to recap — action items: Jordan send runbook and security docs; Priya to schedule deep-dive; Marcus to provision staging; Starlake to provide prompts and security answers. We'll tentatively schedule the deep-dive for next Wednesday, I'll propose 3 slots. Anything else?
[09:58] Aisha: Nothing else, thanks everyone. excited to get started.
[10:02] Jordan: Thanks all, talk soon.

End of transcript.
